key_insight: This paper argues that ad-hoc teamwork should not assume a partner’s abilities are known or fixed to one task. Instead, agents can estimate what a partner is actually capable of and adapt collaboration across different tasks and behaviors.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between standard ad-hoc teamwork assumptions and real-world collaboration, where partner capabilities are hidden and humans may use multiple valid but sub-optimal strategies. The goal is to enable agents to work effectively with novel partners without prior capability labels or task-specific tuning.
method: Estimate partner capabilities from observed interactions rather than assuming them upfront.
Use capability estimates to guide task-agnostic adaptation across different collaboration settings.
Handle uncertainty and diverse partner strategies instead of relying on a single fixed model of the partner.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes collaborative agents more robust in realistic environments where partners vary in skill and strategy. It can improve generalization to new teammates, reduce brittle task-specific assumptions, and support more reliable human-AI teamwork.

paper_title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
paper_authors: Peter Tisnikar, Maja Swieczkowska, Benteng Ma, Gerard Canal, Matteo Leonetti
